title: His piano bought on 125th Street in 1928 and its tuner
summary: He rented then bought a piano in 1928; a Black tuner spent whole days voicing it so it sounded like velvet.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, as you know, there is no convenience much here. I think they have a piano here.
They do, they do -- I just found out.
Downstairs there. Fourth floor, I think; I think they have a piano down there.
Yeah.
Well, I intend to get down there and see what condition it is in soon, and if it's in nice condition, well, then, who knows -- I may knock off one for this particular thing.
Good, good. All right, and as soon as this winter weather calms down and you're back up in Wortsboro, you've got your own beautiful piano, and that's
yours ... that's your soul mate. Yeah. Gosh, do you know how long I've had that piano?
How long?
Make one guess, just one guess. Just for fun.
Okay. Fifty years.
I got it in 1928.
I was right on the button, almost if you had asked me that question before January lst! I missed by three weeks, son of a gun -- teriffic! How did you get that piano, do you remember?

I got it on 125th Street, a store was there; not Lyons and Healey, but another store was there, and I just went and took it for rental, and they sent the piano over, I paid -- and then worked out an arrangement to buy it with what I paid for it, plus some, so that's the way it happened.
Its tone is magnificent.

Well, it's in good shape -- oh, I can -- it's soft, and -- see, because I had a fellow and dig this now -- I had a fellow, he was a colored fellow, and he would spend an entire day on that piano, an entire day --
Tuning it.
Tuning it -- everything he saw
to it, just picking the felts, so when you played, it just sounded like velvet.
Um ...
Oh, when he left, and he would have dinner there, I would fix dinner for him, because he was there all day, he would never leave until he finished tuning it.
And you haven't found a craftsman since like that, either.
Not like that.
Isn't that a shame?
No, not like that.
You know ...
He's the reason for it being in the condition it's in now. He helped it so much, during the time that he was with me -- the deterioration hasn't taken over as much as it would have without his help.

When you said that the sound was like velvet, that is such a good description of how I feel about your touch on the piano -- when you play the piano, I could have my eyes blindfolded, and they could play one person, right after another, and I could pick you out instantly, intuitively; instantly.
Yeah?
Keep going.
